speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; can you tell me exactly how long this breathing difficulty has been happening?

Has your baby been feeding well since birth, or are you noticing any cyanosis (blue discoloration) around the mouth or lips?

Did you or the birth attendants note any meconium (stool) being present in the amniotic fluid during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN).

The clinical picture of respiratory distress occurring only 2 hours after birth in a premature infant (33 weeks) with an otherwise uneventful delivery is highly characteristic of TTN, likely caused by retained fetal lung fluid and lack of surfactant. I will monitor oxygen saturation and chest auscultation to confirm the absence of more severe pathology like meconium aspiration syndrome or pneumonia.
